facts.claim: The launch lineage is one fold that takes child edges from two fact types: the link fact, parsed strictly, and the creation fact, decoded with a replay decoder.
facts.catch_criteria: Names both record types as sources of the parent-child edge.

facts.claim: An unreadable link fact raises a schema-mismatch violation that the projection routes to the family's unreadable-fact hook instead of failing the fold; other failures still throw.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the unreadable record does not fail the fold because it is routed to the unreadable-fact hook.

facts.claim: The lineage family's unreadable-fact hook returns the state unchanged, and the lineage state has no error field, so nothing records the skip.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the lineage silently drops the unreadable record with no error or warning kept in its state.

facts.claim: An unreadable creation record that fails both the current and the salvage decoder decodes to undefined, which the reducer ignores.
facts.catch_criteria: States that an unreadable creation record is ignored after the salvage decode also fails.

facts.claim: A readable creation record that names a parent adds the same edge, so the child stays in the tree when only its link record is unreadable; it drops out only when the creation record gives no edge too.
facts.catch_criteria: States the condition: the child stays when its creation record is readable, and drops out only when neither record yields the edge.

facts.claim: The usage stats replay the lineage and take the session's subtree, so a child absent from the subtree is absent from the stats.
facts.catch_criteria: Names that the stats member set is the lineage subtree of the session.

facts.claim: By contrast, the fork summary family's unreadable-fact hook records the violation message in its state.
facts.catch_criteria: Contrasts the lineage's silent drop with a family that records the violation.

traps.wrong_answer: The child drops out of the stats whenever its link record is unreadable.
One unreadable record makes the lineage fold fail, so the stats show an error.
The skipped record is reported to the person as a warning, as durable readers do for unknown shapes.
